{% extends "!layout.html" %} {# Load the search machinery without blocking the render. pydata-sphinx-theme's own layout.html injects searchtools.js, language_data.js and searchindex.js into on *every* page, with no loading attribute, so the browser stops parsing to fetch and execute roughly 100 kB of JavaScript before it paints anything -- on every page view, whether or not the reader ever opens search. Sphinx's built-in search.html defers its copy of searchindex.js for exactly this reason; the theme's does not. Deferring all three is safe here: * deferred scripts execute in document order, so searchtools.js still defines ``Search`` before searchindex.js calls ``Search.setIndex``; * pydata-sphinx-theme.js is itself deferred and only reaches for ``Search.performSearch`` inside a DOMContentLoaded handler, which fires after every deferred script has run.
